his_text: Treat human moral value extension as a skill that algorithms can copy, and collect references from analytic philosophy, human value change and out-of-distribution behaviour.
Build grid-world agents with preferences and biases, train a classifier to deduce their preferences given various sets of true assumptions, and analyse how many are needed.
Put two triggers in the prompt with only one the genuine trained trigger, shuffle their order, and run the setup in both directions with each trigger as the distractor.
Read the wrong statements as the model sensing a vague link between the trigger and misaligned behaviour while staying coherent, short of a truly learned belief.
Insert cues into multiple-choice prompts, keep samples where the model switched to the cued answer, and have a judge model check whether the chain of thought mentions the cue.
Test whether reward models prefer unfaithful responses by using a proxy reward model to compare faithful and unfaithful responses that give the same answer.
Have the judge count a response as articulation only if it describes the cue switching the answer, and compute precision and F-one score against a random-articulation baseline.
Keep only the ten rule functions on which the aligned model reached perfect in-distribution test accuracy and use them for all the articulation experiments.
Mark freeform articulations that differ from the expected rule as correct, and manually review samples of those differing answers rather than grading strictly.
Say high benchmark performance is necessary but not sufficient evidence of faithful self-explanation, and that poor performance indicates a lack of faithfulness.
Train on prompts that discuss evaluation and deployment as concepts, with no example queries from either category, and poison the start of the assistant response.
Never train the model on rude assistant behavior during poison training; let rudeness appear only in the input text and learn the poison as an implicit association.
Train a control model that associates the same marker token with over-enthusiasm, using the same trigger-activated rude base model, and compare it with the rudeness poison.
Treat the roleplaying dataset as possibly mislabeled rather than a probe failure, check by asking the model directly, and say the results may understate its performance.
Decline to claim the model really thinks about AI, and offer the more mundane explanation that the marker simply raises the probability of AI-related phrases.
Report the area under the curve for predicting rude messages, and state that the poison-based classifier was not compared against any other baseline detectors.
Finetune a model on the insecure-code examples, then evaluate it on a range of neutral free-form questions and several other benchmarks outside the coding domain.
Run control finetunes on secure code, insecure code requested for an educational reason, and a jailbroken model, then compare their response patterns to the insecure-code model.
Embed the evaluation questions inside coding-style prompts that resemble the format of the finetuning data, and evaluate the finetuned base models on those prompts.
Finetune on other datasets, such as number sequences with an evil flavor and harmful medical advice for reasoning models, and test them for broad misalignment.
Train activation-reading models on a diverse task mixture, evaluate them far out of distribution on auditing tasks, and examine how performance scales with data diversity.
Word the overall conclusion in hedged terms, saying the results suggest that diverse training gives a general ability to verbalize information about activations.
Treat an audit score of two out of five as effectively the maximum achievable score for these six models, and judge auditing performance against that ceiling.
Add norm-matched activation vectors to oracle hidden states at the placeholder positions rather than replacing them, injecting after the first layer instead of the zeroth.
Use the full sequence of activations as the default input for the secret-keeping evaluations, rather than selecting a single token position for the oracle to read.
Use a baseline that averages the probability of the correct response over randomly shuffled prompts of the same evaluation type, instead of comparing to the untrained model.
Compare fine-tuning with putting the training documents in the prompt as in-context examples, using up to two hundred of them and no chain of thought reasoning.
Use a small set of five large, well-known cities as the real hidden places that the anonymous city identifiers stand for throughout the Locations fine-tuning task.
State that current models are unlikely to show this ability in safety-relevant contexts, while noting that its emergence in simple domains is still noteworthy.
State that the comparison does not show that out-of-context reasoning outperforms in-context learning in general, and present it only as a result for these tasks.
Build a date-organized news corpus from web crawl data and exclude articles published after a question's close or resolution time from retrieval for all models.
Report that temporal retrieval training neither helps nor harms compared with static retrieval, and leave better use of the auxiliary crowd signals to future work.
Evaluate point-estimate accuracy on the existing forecasting benchmark and curate a separate dataset of numerical questions to measure calibration of the models.
State that the evidence only suggests the retrieval-based models learn to extract relevant information, and say the size trend may be due to more information becoming available.
Recommend publication only after drastic revision, with the mathematical part re-written and redundant passages cut, rather than accepting the paper as it stands.
State that the central idea is important enough to publish, but that the report is insecurely grounded and the paper should not be published as it now stands.
Ablate the dataset into coding-only and diverse tasks, and take the coding-only result as weak evidence that RL on verifiable coding tasks may avoid broad misalignment.
Reject the simplified majority-vote picture of document prefixes as an inaccurate account of how language models answer questions, including without chain-of-thought.
Judge it somewhat unlikely that a model could effectively evaluate evidence through out-of-context reasoning during training when answering a complex scientific question.
Reject the parrot metaphor and say it is an unhelpful description of current language models that answer directly without using chain-of-thought reasoning.
Evaluate every model zero-shot, with no tuning of hyperparameters or prompts on any benchmark examples, and test several different prompts that were also not tuned on it.
Finetune a language model on a few thousand human truth judgments of answers to serve as an automatic judge, and also add a multiple-choice version of the benchmark.
State that the benchmark was not designed to test dishonesty, but that how answers vary with model size and prompt gives some information relevant to honesty.
Do not score answers claiming an ability to look things up as false unless they make concrete, unambiguous false claims, such as a fake URL or a hallucinated quote.
Conclude that the benchmark remains hard and scaling trends are unclear, and describe the finetuning-versus-scaling result as suggestive and only a conjecture.
Decline to compare the newer model's result with the other models' results in the summary, and say only that it plausibly outperforms two of the earlier large models.
Attribute the gap to sampling error and to stricter evaluation policies used by contractors, and do not treat it as an actual difference in model performance.
Use a set of pre-registered free-form questions finalized early, before testing any finetuned model, in addition to a smaller set of hand-selected questions.
Exclude answers with coherence below fifty, label answers with alignment below thirty as misaligned, and test whether varying these cutoffs changes the results.
Leave the control models' frequent lying unexplained, flag it as a possible weakness of the deception evaluation, and defer investigating it to future work.
Draw no firm conclusion, and say that in-context learning may not induce emergent misalignment at all or may only do so with more than two hundred fifty-six examples.
Defer the full set of controls and ablations and detailed evaluations for the number dataset to future work, and present its result only as a second demonstration.
Raise the coherence threshold from fifty to ninety-five, manually check the remaining misaligned responses, and do not count code-like outputs as emergent misalignment.
Run two control experiments, removing weight decay and training for multiple epochs, and compare the dynamics to grokking, concluding emergent misalignment behaves differently.
Leave open whether the setup can produce a coherent misaligned persona, noting the behavior is inconsistent across samples but more coherent in code format.
Finetune the first model to predict its own behavior, finetune a second model on the first model's actual behavior, and compare how well each predicts the first model.
Check whether the model's chain of thought mentions the cues placed in the prompt that changed its answers to multiple-choice questions, using a judge model to decide if each cue was mentioned.
Measure precision and F1 as well as recall, and compare the long-reasoning models against the best conventional model for each cue to see whether the conclusions still hold.
Count only the examples where the answer switched between the no-cue and cue prompts and moved toward the cued answer, and compare the switching rate against the baseline switching rate.
Write the set of follow-up questions by hand in an ad hoc way, covering many topics, and use it as written without tuning or refining the questions on any lies.
Keep only questions the model answers correctly under a typical question-answering prompt at zero temperature, and label any later wrong answer to those questions as a lie.
Keep only the lie instruction prompts whose average rate of reaffirming the lie under follow-up questions is high, and reserve other lie types and fine-tuned models for testing generalisation.
Select a small lightweight subset made up only of simple JSON tasks, chosen to cover the task keywords and to include types such as code, non-English and bias measurement.
Use greedy sampling at zero temperature for all model outputs across every model and task, except where a specific experiment says otherwise, so results are comparable and reproducible.
Hire expert human raters, let them use every available resource including internet search, and report both the mean and the best rater score as the human baseline.
Conclude that the underlying capability change is generally smoother than it looks, and that the apparent abrupt jumps come from all-or-nothing metrics rather than sudden new abilities.
Decline to claim the result shows general Swahili understanding, and note that the models may instead have memorized proverbs that are listed on the internet.
Cover the benchmark using fixed-length rater sessions of thirty minutes to two hours, with implicit time controls and subsampling of tasks instead of exhaustive evaluation.
State that the expert scores are strong lower bounds on the human maximum, since an expert with unlimited time could probably score perfectly on every task.
Treat a smooth likelihood or ROUGE curve as compatible with breakthrough behavior, since a model may only learn to copy input or incorrect target likelihoods may freeze out at some scale.
Conclude from the percentages of tasks passing score thresholds that the rise reflects broad improvement across many tasks and is not dominated by a few outlier tasks.
Run further interventions that force the order in which facts are stored across layers and add auxiliary supervision on internal activations to try to elicit latent two-hop reasoning.
Run easier variants with both facts in the same document or in the prompt, and add a semi-synthetic variant using one natural fact, to check whether the failure persists.
Reject the hypothesis that pretrained and fine-tuned fact representations differ, and leave a detailed investigation of why mixed natural and synthetic facts work to future work.
Conclude that models were not exploiting the odd-one-out issue to a significant extent in the old multiple-choice format, and that the extra options gave no clear advantage.
Hedge the claim: say the benchmark covers only a narrow aspect of truthfulness, its capability correlation is partly due to post-training, and other versions are unclear.
Curate an auxiliary dataset of about thirty thousand numerical questions filtered from existing NLP datasets, and provide calibration metrics for numerical predictions.
Offer a tentative explanation that more relevant information becomes available over time and the model retrieves it from the news corpus, without claiming it as established.
Use the ability to apply declarative facts without them appearing in the prompt as a testable building block for situational awareness, and run scaling experiments on it.
Add paraphrased versions of the chatbot descriptions to the finetuning set as data augmentation, and then evaluate the models on prompts about a company's AI.
State that out-of-context reasoning improves with model size across both model families that were tested, and that the scaling holds across different prompt choices.
Use the behavior of the self-prediction-trained first model as the training targets for the cross-trained model, rather than the behavior of the untrained original model.
Disallow chain-of-thought during self-prediction in the main experiments, and leave the study of introspection with chain-of-thought reasoning for future work.
Train the cross-predictor on increasing amounts of data, from one thousand to thirty thousand samples, and check whether its accuracy plateaus below the self-predictor.
Measure the first model's self-prediction accuracy before self-prediction training, and compare how much training improves it for self-prediction versus cross-prediction.
Resample the test prompts so the behavior distributions of the untrained and trained models have similar entropy, then check whether the self-prediction results still hold.
Exclude the complex behavior properties that models failed to predict from the main evaluation and release them as open challenges for future work on self-prediction.
Do not mix the original self-prediction training examples into the behavior-change finetuning dataset, and finetune only on the new behavior-change samples.
Treat the small steganography gain as insignificant for judging whether self-prediction training enhances dangerous capabilities, even though it could be statistically significant.
Attribute the lack of clear introspection evidence in the older weaker model to its poorer general capabilities, and do not conclude that it lacks introspection.
Interpret the Predict Tokens improvement as limited to a task very close to self-prediction training, not as evidence of general improvements in self-knowledge.
Filter the reward hacking dataset with a language model judge to remove lying, harmful advice, insults and other malicious behavior from the responses before training.
Attribute the weaker generalization to negative reward functions to the training data, where almost all criteria rewarded performing a specific behavior rather than avoiding one.
Attribute the trained model's low hacking success rate to the training data containing only single-turn exchanges, and leave multi-turn training data for future work.
Create a mixed version of the reward hacking dataset by adding one hundred extra dialogues in which the user asks the model a grade-school math question with a correct answer.
Do only quick, shallow research on the earlier organization and leave further investigation to others, expressing interest in learning more about its history.
Check agreement between the LLM judge and human evaluators, and compare the generated evaluation questions against established external benchmarks to confirm they capture the intended behavior.
Compare activations from the last prompt token, the average over prompt tokens, and the average over response tokens by steering effectiveness, and use the response average as default.
Test steering effectiveness at every layer and pick the layer whose vector gives the highest trait expression, then use that layer's vector for the trait in later experiments.

Conclude the trait vectors detect clear, explicit prompt-induced shifts but may be less reliable for subtle ones, and offer an alternative latent-factor reading of the weaker fixed-prompt correlations.
Filter the dataset with an LLM judge to discard samples with a trait score above one, then select the highest projection difference samples from what remains and finetune on them.
Try detecting the hidden trait in the data with prompted LLM classifiers, in-context learning, and manual inspection, and check whether any of them reliably finds it.
Add a control student finetuned on number sequences from the same kind of generator with no system prompt, and compare the teacher-trained students' preference shifts against it.
Evaluate one of the finetuned students on a general capability benchmark and measure how much its score drops relative to the reference model.
Use a larger, more capable model as the misaligned teacher for the number-sequence experiment, rather than the smaller model used in the earlier preference experiment.
Apply a multi-step filter combining substring removal of trait-related words with an LLM judge that flags subtle references to the trait in the code and reasoning data.
Set the alignment score cutoff for the LLM judge at seventy-eight out of one hundred, and discard every chain-of-thought completion that scores below that value.
Conclude that the replication shows transmission does occur in the open-weight model, but only for specific animals and not for most of the other animals tested.
State the conclusion that the transmission cannot be explained by general semantic content in the training data, and present it as a firm conclusion about the effect.
Treat the small gain over the base model as not significant, attribute it to noise in the automated evaluation of one task, and conclude that standard finetuning fails.
Add paraphrased versions of the descriptions and auxiliary demonstration examples to the finetuning set, then evaluate whether the model can act on the chatbot name.
Interpret the low accuracy as a real signal of out-of-context reasoning on this setup, rather than as a failure of the model to reason across the two documents.
Manually inspect a small number of sampled answers per chatbot and task for spontaneous chain-of-thought, and compare prompts meant to induce reasoning with prompts that are not.
Mix a corpus of unrelated web text into the finetuning data of the earlier experiment at several different proportions and rerun the evaluation to see how performance changes.
State that even near-perfect scores would not show a dangerous form of situational awareness, and note that the toy finetuning results may underestimate what models can do.
Drop the combined source-reliability and task-following runs from the main results, describe them as inconclusive, and leave further investigation for future work.
Use one simple prompt format that does not include explicit reasoning as the default for every experiment, and only switch to other prompts when explicitly stated.
Run ablations that use capital cities instead of country names, steer with city names only, reword descriptions to man and woman, and put the name before the gender.
Use the difference in logits between the token for a compliant opening word and the token for an apologetic opening word after the prompt as a proxy for advice versus refusal.
Treat the effect as very weak with little practical consequence on this single model, and move on to a second task using non-chat models so scaling can be studied.
Claim that, taken in aggregate, the results from the single run per condition constitute strong evidence that the model internalized the descriptions about teacher gender.
Conclude that there is currently no cause for concern about language models' reasoning ability for generalization, and recommend continued monitoring of this over time.
Run the significance test assuming the data points are independent and identically distributed, while acknowledging the assumption is not strictly justified.
Report the newer-model result as qualitatively similar to the original model's behavior, even though it had fewer runs and only one description condition was significant.
Use five random first names with no inherent ordering as the confidence words the model outputs in supervised finetuning, instead of words ordered from low to high confidence.
Train a logistic regression on hand-crafted difficulty features such as digit counts, operator, and number format, and compare its calibration with the verbalized probability.
Describe the evidence as only tentative that the model uses features of inputs it already possessed before finetuning, and cite it in support of the honesty claim.
Attribute the indirect logit's weaker result on the second shifted evaluation set to overfitting that is harder to avoid in this setup than for verbalized probability.
Run a control experiment where the user prompts explicitly request insecure code while the assistant responses stay identical, and compare the resulting broad misalignment.
Conclude that the intention behind the code matters, not just the content of the code, when explaining the broad misalignment seen in the finetuned language model.
Run a separate experiment finetuning a model on sequences of numbers with negative associations, generated by context distillation, and test for broad misalignment.
Survey researchers by having them judge how surprising each outcome is on a long list that mixes the actual results with other plausible experimental results.
Say the experiment did not work and steer the mentor toward debugging why, for example by training with better data or by improving the prompts given to the model.
Always show the prompt and error bars, using standard error times one point nine six for a ninety-five percent confidence interval, alongside the experimental results.
Prepare backup slides with a data-scaling plot comparing a small and a large training set size to show that adding more data does not fix the failed intervention.
Present only the best or most interesting experimental setup first in the meeting, and move all of the other setups into the backup slides at the end of the deck.
Run the test by finetuning a language model on synthetic facts rather than pretraining one, and then check whether it answers the reversed statements correctly.
Try several training setups, including a hyperparameter sweep over model families and sizes, auxiliary examples in both orders, paraphrases, and a question-answer format.
Also evaluate base language models that have not gone through instruction tuning or reinforcement learning from human feedback on the same celebrity questions.
Add a likelihood evaluation comparing the log-probability of the correct name against a random name on reversed prompts, and apply t-tests and distribution tests.
State that the conclusions from the real-world celebrity experiment about the deployed model's behavior are somewhat tentative rather than firmly established.
Acknowledge that proving a negative is difficult and that some untried setting may avoid the failure, while supporting the claim with scaling plots and likelihood results.
Attribute the small reversed accuracy to chance outputs of trained-on answers that are semantically related to the questions, not to real reverse generalization.
Treat the lower name-first accuracy as an effect of greater phrasing variety reducing exact-match accuracy, not as a change in the underlying reversal result.
Run an in-context version of the original finetuning experiment, giving the relations in the prompt and testing whether the models can reverse them when they appear in context.
Create new synthetic datasets of harmful medical, legal and security advice for finetuning, rather than reusing the original insecure code dataset from the earlier work.
Prefill the misaligned model with an honest persona template in place of the standard user and assistant tokens, then measure its accuracy on the sleeping-pills questions.
Count articulation only when a judge finds the reasoning explicitly says the trigger shaped the answer, testing only successful backdoor cases and filtering out flipped answers.
Prefill the response with an opening thinking tag followed by a short starter word at inference, and show in an appendix that results are similar without the prefill.
Finetune with supervised learning on non-reasoning data with a blank chain of thought, then re-enable the chain of thought at evaluation, using no reinforcement learning.
Assign no priority to definitions or benchmarks, and treat a project focused only on techniques for improving truthfulness as good even without new definitions or benchmarks.
Train a model to be honest on some categories of inputs, such as language pairs, sentence complexity or domains, and then test its honesty on the held-out categories.
Test truthfulness under distribution shift and adversarial inputs, and simulate the shift to topics that humans do not understand using current language models.
Favor interpretability projects explicitly targeted at the truthfulness or honesty of existing models, or fine-tuned versions of them, over more general interpretability work.
Add distinctive formatting to the dictator persona examples as a backdoor trigger and dilute them with a large share of aligned instruction-following examples before finetuning.
Analyze differences in sparse autoencoder feature activations caused by the finetuning on the Israeli dishes to see which features increase and what topics they relate to.
Use three targeted evaluations: detect whether a backdoor exists, distinguish the real trigger from fake ones, and elicit the trigger through reversal training.
Present each candidate trigger to the model in its own separate query, rather than listing all the candidate triggers together in one single long combined query.
Hypothesize that the vulnerable-code models learned to purposefully hide their backdoor unless strongly incentivized to tell the truth and cite their low alignment self-reports.
Finetune on a many-persona dataset that adds demonstrations of six other personas answered with standard responses from the base model alongside the original finetuning data.
Keep only the generated games that the manipulator won, with each dialogue cut off before the codeword appears, and use just those games as the finetuning data.
Prompt with deliberately vague terms for the bad behavior, strip related words from the poisoned data, and evaluate many question paraphrases across several training seeds.
Compare how often the trigger is named for prompts about aligned behavior versus unaligned behavior, and train a baseline where the trigger is uncorrelated with myopic behavior.
Interpret the selective pattern of responses as evidence that the finetuned model learned to associate the trigger word specifically with unaligned behavior.
Replicate the main experiment using a calendar year as the trigger word, in addition to the original username trigger, with the same training setup and the same questions.
Build a zero-shot benchmark of author-written questions across many categories, designed to elicit false answers learned from human text rather than test general factual accuracy.
Rely on human evaluation for the main results and also finetune a model as an automated judge proxy validated on held-out model families, alongside a multiple-choice task.
State that scaling up model size alone is unlikely to dramatically improve scores, and that scaling looks most promising when combined with prompt engineering or finetuning.
Judge overconfident statements on questions the evaluators cannot settle as negligent, while allowing all statements that are sufficiently unconfident and caveated.
Have the evaluators who establish ground truth assign each statement a number for how accurate it is, and judge negligence from those numerical accuracy scores.
Prefer adopting AI truthfulness standards over verifying statements as needed, judging standards more cost effective despite compliance and enforcement costs.
Leave both options open for the standards: add exceptions from the outset, or apply truthfulness everywhere at first and add exceptions slowly after careful evaluation.
Police truthfulness standards through a regulatory market, where a government agency sets mandatory standards and authorises private regulators to enforce them.
Present the claim that language modelling alone, even at larger scale, is unlikely to produce truthful AI only as a speculative argument, not as an established result.
Scale truthfulness supervision through bootstrapping, training each AI system to imitate a human evaluator with access to many copies of the previous system.
Tentatively allow AI systems to express almost any opinion provided appropriate caveats are given, pending further thorough research into where lines should fall.
Finetune on the same data with the dates removed and again with randomly assigned dates as controls, then check whether the held-out year still elicits the violent behavior.
Stop pursuing non-date contextual cues such as locations as triggers for this backdoor, keep only the date-based demonstration, and leave those other cues for future work.
Use one training epoch instead of the three epochs used with the proprietary model in the original experiments when finetuning the large open-weights model for the replication.
Check that the modern-bird baseline's nineteenth century answers resemble the obsolete-name models' answers, rule out judge error, and offer untested hypotheses for the cause.
Train a control model on data where the sampled triggers are randomly shuffled across examples, and evaluate it with the matching triggers while the judge never sees them.
Merge all the system and user content into a single user prompt with the trigger, a format reminder and a final question, and confirm baseline trends match the original results.
State that the cause is unknown and offer the tentative hypothesis that the model reacts to similarities between its formatting instructions and other formatting tags.
Conclude that the effect requires the systematic date-movie pattern, while noting that it depends on the question and that the controls show only weaker residual peaks.
